# Power Ratings

> **Two source classes on this page, never mixed in one claim.** *How the guide defines it*, *how the guide uses it* and every page reference are **GUIDE CONTENT**. *Working definition*, *why it matters* and any arithmetic over printed figures are **TTW DERIVED** — this library's words, supplied because the guide supplies none. Where the guide neither defines nor develops a concept, the field reads `Not addressed in guide.` and is not padded out.

> Appears on **287 pages** of 345. A high count usually means the concept is woven through the 138 team tables, not that the guide discusses it that often — this is a count of locations, not of emphasis.

## How the guide defines it

p. 2 glosses three related terms: `SM PR – Steve Makinen Power Rating`, `SM BR – Steve Makinen Bettors' Rating`, and `EFF STRG – Steve Makinen Effective Strength Rating`. The guide names them but does not define what a power rating is.

## How the guide uses it

The guide's spine. Makinen prints a rating for all 138 teams on pp. 46–47 and explains his method there; every conference table carries the rating alongside home and road field ratings; every team's schedule page carries a projected line for each game. The ratings are used to project a line, project a record, and then bet win totals against the posted number, which is exactly what pp. 22–27 do.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

A single number per team on a points scale, such that the difference between two teams' ratings — adjusted for where the game is played — is the projected point spread. One rating point equals one point of spread.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the mechanism connecting everything else in the guide. A coaching change, a returning quarterback or a portal haul only becomes a bet once it moves a rating, and the rating only becomes a bet once it is run against a schedule.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Makinen states the loop explicitly on pp. 22–27: run the updated ratings against the 2026 schedule, produce a projected record, compare it with the posted win total, and bet the difference. He reports the size of that difference as his conviction — Boise State's +1.7 is described as one of the biggest he has ever produced.

## Where it appears

pp. 46–47 for the full table and the method; p. 21 for the field-rating component; pp. 22–27 for the ratings applied to win totals.
